newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Sept retail sales rise 0.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Sept retail sales rise 0.2 pct.

text.p: Canadian retail sales rose 0.2 percent in September to a seasonally adjusted C$17.93 billion from an upwardly revised C$17.89 billion in August, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
Sales, ex vehicles, s/a +0.1 +0.8 C$13.65 bln
A Reuter survey of economists had forecast that seasonally adjusted retail sales would rise by 0.4 percent in August. The agency said early indications for October were for a rise.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast a 0.4 percent increase in retail trade in September.

Statistics Canada said the slight increase in retail sales in September was in line with the slow growth seen since the end of 1995. During the first nine months of this year, retail sales rose 1.4 percent from the same period last year.

"As reported in the media, job insecurity, high consumer debt and weak personal incomes may have restrained the positive impact of recently declining interest rates on consumer spending," the government agency said.
The consumer confidence index, as measured by the Conference Board of Canada, also declined in the third quarter.

In September, retail sales were higher in the "other semi-durable goods" sector, such as book and hardware stores, as well as the automotive sector. Sales of furniture and drugs also rose in the month.
Sales of clothes remained flat in September and sales of food and general merchandise declined in the month.
